classification.difficultyReason: Select suitable auxiliary forms from coefficient signs and solve on shifted intervals, accounting for repeated endpoints and the amplitude-equality case.

content.prompt: Solve the following for $0^\circ\le x\le360^\circ$, correct to the nearest degree.

answer.worked:
For $R\sin(x+\alpha)$, equating coefficients gives $R\cos\alpha=\sqrt3$ and $R\sin\alpha=1$. Thus $R=\sqrt{3+1}=2$ and $\alpha=30^\circ$ in the first quadrant.
$$\sqrt3\sin x+\cos x=2\sin(x+30^\circ).$$
Since $30^\circ\le x+30^\circ\le390^\circ$,
$$\begin{align*}2\sin(x+30^\circ)&=1\\\sin(x+30^\circ)&=\frac12\\x+30^\circ&=30^\circ,\ 150^\circ,\ 390^\circ\\x&=0^\circ,\ 120^\circ,\ 360^\circ.\end{align*}$$

For $R\cos(x-\alpha)$, equating coefficients gives $R\cos\alpha=8$ and $R\sin\alpha=15$. Thus $R=\sqrt{8^2+15^2}=17$ and $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{15}{8}\right)$ in the first quadrant.
$$8\cos x+15\sin x=17\cos(x-\alpha).$$
Since $-\alpha\le x-\alpha\le360^\circ-\alpha$, the only angle in this interval with cosine $1$ is $0^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}17\cos(x-\alpha)&=17\\\cos(x-\alpha)&=1\\x-\alpha&=0^\circ\\x&=\alpha\approx61.92751^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=62^\circ$, to the nearest degree.

For $R\sin(x-\alpha)$, equating coefficients gives $R\cos\alpha=3$ and $R\sin\alpha=3$. Thus $R=\sqrt{3^2+3^2}=3\sqrt2$ and $\alpha=45^\circ$.
$$3\sin x-3\cos x=3\sqrt2\sin(x-45^\circ).$$
The shifted interval is $-45^\circ\le x-45^\circ\le315^\circ$. Let $\beta=\sin^{-1}\!\left(\frac{4}{3\sqrt2}\right)$.
$$\begin{align*}3\sqrt2\sin(x-45^\circ)&=4\\\sin(x-45^\circ)&=\frac{4}{3\sqrt2}\\x-45^\circ&=\beta,\ 180^\circ-\beta\\x&=45^\circ+\beta,\ 225^\circ-\beta\\x&\approx115.52878^\circ,\ 154.47122^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=116^\circ,\ 154^\circ$, to the nearest degree.

$x=23^\circ,\ 244^\circ$.

Transform to a single cosine and solve in the shifted interval.
answer.worked:
For $R\cos(x+\alpha)$, equating coefficients gives $R\cos\alpha=20$ and $R\sin\alpha=21$. Thus $R=\sqrt{20^2+21^2}=29$ and $\alpha=\tan^{-1}\!\left(\frac{21}{20}\right)$ in the first quadrant.
$$20\cos x-21\sin x=29\cos(x+\alpha).$$
The shifted interval is $\alpha\le x+\alpha\le360^\circ+\alpha$. Let $\beta=\cos^{-1}\!\left(\frac{10}{29}\right)$.
$$\begin{align*}29\cos(x+\alpha)&=10\\\cos(x+\alpha)&=\frac{10}{29}\\x+\alpha&=\beta,\ 360^\circ-\beta\\x&=\beta-\alpha,\ 360^\circ-\beta-\alpha\\x&\approx23.43155^\circ,\ 243.77409^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=23^\circ,\ 244^\circ$, to the nearest degree.
